excerpt: To scrape a web page, you only need two things: Your API key... The encoded web page URL you want to scrape
This can be useful for scraping a Single Page Application built with frameworks such as React.js, Angular.js, JQuery or Vue.
If you want to interact with pages you want to scrape before we return your the HTML you can add JavaScript scenario to your API call.
Our headless browsers will wait for the CSS / Xpath selector passed in the parameter before returning the HTML.
By default, ScrapingBee does not block ads. To avoid scraping them (e.g.,to speed up your request), use `block_ads=true`
By default, and to speed up requests, ScrapingBee blocks all images and CSS in the scraped page, but to scrape them, use `block_resources=false`
If you need to change the dimension of the browser's viewport (window) when scraping the target page you can use the `window_width` and `window_height` parameters.
extract_rules [stringified JSON] ("") Data extraction from CSS selectors
ai_query [string] ("") The information you want to extract from the webpage using AI
premium_proxy [boolean] (false) Use premium proxies to bypass difficult to scrape websites
country_code [string] ("") Premium proxy geolocation
session_id [integer] ("") Route multiple API requests through the same IP address
screenshot_selector [string] ("") Return a screenshot of a particular area of the page, targeted by a CSS selector
mode [string] ("") Let ScrapingBee pick the cheapest configuration that succeeds. Only value is auto
return_page_markdown [boolean] (false) Return the page content in markdown format
The API will then respond with the raw HTML content of the target URL:
By default, ScrapingBee fetches the URL to scrape via a headless browser that will execute the JavaScript code on the page.
